Name: PZL_C1_CustomsCage
setup: A steel mesh customs cage with a four-digit keypad. Pruitt's team case is visible through the mesh from two rooms away. He set the code himself, assuming the next federal agent through here would watch the dock office tape before reaching the cage.
solution: Enter 0214 on the keypad - the timestamp of the first fragment of the security footage, which the scratched note 'CAGE = WHEN IT OPENED' tells you to use.
failure: No lockout and no alarm, but the keypad is loud. Every third wrong entry spawns two Husks at the warehouse apron door and sets them to investigate the cage, so guessing costs ammunition instead of progress.
hint_1: A customs cage is where they put the things they don't want walking off. Four digits, so it's a date or a time to somebody.
hint_2: There's writing scratched by the keypad. Whoever set the code left you the sentence, not the number.
hint_3: When it opened. You watched it open. Put the time on the keypad - zero two one four.
hint_trigger: Hint 1 at 45 s at the keypad; hint 2 at 90 s or 2 wrong entries; hint 3 at 150 s, 4 wrong entries, or a second return to the cage. If FLG_C1_TapeWatched is unset, hint 3 becomes 'Go back to the office and watch the night log first.'

Name: PZL_C1_CranePower
setup: Two stages in one room. The gantry supply panel has an empty 400 A fuse carrier, so nothing works until the spare cartridge is fetched from the break room cabinet. With the fuse seated, three brass-plated switches labelled C1, C2 and C3 go live under the main breaker, and must be thrown in the supervisor's start-up order. The yard gate motor and the yard crane are on the same bus.
solution: Seat KEY_C1_Fuse in the carrier, then throw C3, then C1, then C2. The rota board says to bring up whoever is on shift now and then go round the clock; it is 22:40, so nights (Crane 3) first, then day (Crane 1), then swing (Crane 2).
failure: A wrong order trips the main breaker. The lights die, the bang spikes Leon's noise radius, the switches lock out for 30 seconds, and Husks are pathed to the control house door - two on the first trip, three on the second, four on every trip after. The puzzle never fails permanently; brute-forcing all six permutations just arrives at the Hookman out of ammunition.
hint_1: Dead panel means a pulled fuse. Nobody keeps a spare in a shed that floods - try where they make tea.
hint_2: Three switches, three cranes, and a supervisor who wrote the start-up order on the rota board. Whoever's on shift comes up first.
hint_3: It's the middle of the night, Cater. Nights is Crane 3. Then round the clock - day, then swing. Three, one, two.
hint_trigger: Hint 1 at 40 s at a dead panel (suppressed if the player already holds KEY_C1_Fuse) or 60 s at a live panel; hint 2 at 120 s with the fuse seated or 1 breaker trip; hint 3 at 200 s or 2 breaker trips.

Name: PZL_C1_DropZone
setup: The boss arena's trick, solved during the fight. A 20-foot container hangs on the yard crane's hook block over a hazard-striped square of concrete, and a release lever sits at the crane leg with two lit bulbs for its two remaining uses. The Hookman will not walk onto the square on his own; the player has to bait him across it.
solution: Bait the Hookman fully inside the hazard square - stand on it and move off late, or draw a hook throw from the far side so he closes across it - then pull the lever at the crane leg. The drop pins him and exposes the growth on his back for about 6 seconds. Two uses only; after that, finish him by baiting the hook into steel and shooting the back during the 2.5 s overreach.
failure: Pulling the lever while he is off the square wastes one of the two uses: the container hits bare concrete and an indicator bulb goes out. Standing on the square yourself when it drops is an instant kill, which the sign, Varga's note and the lit stripes all warn about beforehand.
hint_1: Don't trade with him. He's got twelve feet of reach and you've got a handgun.
hint_2: He throws that hook and when it bites steel instead of you, he can't let go. Watch his back when he's pulling.
hint_3: There's a container hanging over those painted stripes and a lever at the crane leg. Get him on the stripes and pull it.
hint_trigger: Hint 1 at 20 s of fighting; hint 2 at 60 s or after two completed hook throws; hint 3 at 110 s, on Leon dropping to Danger health, or after the player passes within 2 m of the lever twice without using it.

Name: PZL_C2_OrganHymn
setup: The chapel organ is the only working machine on the island. Its keyboards are swollen shut; only the lettered foot pedals move. A wooden shutter over the small pipes runs on the bell tower latch linkage, and Calder hid the bell tower key inside it three weeks ago. Interacting opens a focus view of eight lettered pedals and a six-slot readout.
solution: Press the pedals D, G, E, D, A, D in that order (hymn 42 "Low Tide", pedal line, six notes left to right as written). The pipe shutter draws back and the bell tower key is on a nail inside.
failure: A wrong pedal plays the flat chord, which is extremely loud, and resets the entry. The second cumulative mistake in a visit brings two Drowned up the flooded nave; each further mistake brings one more, capped at four alive. The chancel platform is high ground, so the fight is winnable. Death respawns at the vestry safe room with the sequence reset and the sheet never lost.
hint_1: That organ's the only thing in the parish that still works. If the doctor hid something, she hid it in the thing nobody would dare touch.
hint_2: Ignore the keyboards, they're swollen shut. The verger's note on the bench says pedals only, and the sheet from her cellar is the pedal line.
hint_3: Six pedals, left to right as written: D, G, E, D, A, and D again. People drop the last one. Don't.
hint_trigger: Hint 1 after 60 s in the nave with KEY_C2_HymnSheet held and the puzzle untouched. Hint 2 after 2 failed attempts or 150 s with the puzzle open. Hint 3 after 4 failed attempts or 240 s. Timers pause during combat and no hint repeats within a visit.

Name: PZL_C2_LensReveal
setup: A three-panel lens drum in the lamp room, each panel on its own salt-seized worm drive with a brass bearing dial reading 000 to 355 in 5 degree steps. No handle is supplied: the keeper's crank has been down at the fish market cold store since March. The service door is behind the keeper's framed chart and has no keyhole, because the latch inside its frame is a bimetal strip that releases when the concentrated beam warms it.
solution: With KEY_C2_LensCrank fitted, set the lower mirror to 040 (chapel spire), then the middle to 115 (sluice gate housing), then the upper to 250 (drowned mooring stone). The three beams gather on the worn brass patch under the chart, the latch drops, and the chart panel opens onto the hidden stair.
failure: No enemies and no death. A wrong bearing just puts the beam on bare wall. Touching a higher spindle before the one below it is correct shears the drive pin: a bang, that dial jams for 20 s, and all three dials reset to 000. Three shears in a row bends the crank lug, adding a 4 s wind-up to every turn for the rest of the chapter. Without the crank the spindles do not move at all.
hint_1: There's no keyhole on that service door, is there. So the lock isn't a lock, it's the light.
hint_2: The keeper's book sets each mirror on a landmark, lower then middle then upper. His third bearing's scratched out, but the harbor master's chart has all three.
hint_3: Lower to the spire, 040. Middle to the sluice, 115. Upper to the drowned mooring stone, 250. In that order or you'll shear the pin.
hint_trigger: Hint 1 after 60 s in the lamp room. Hint 2 after 2 shears or 150 s. Hint 3 after 4 shears or 240 s, and only if FLG_C2_BearingsKnown is set; otherwise hint 2 repeats once and names the harbor master's hut, because Mara cannot know a number Leon has not read out.

Name: PZL_C2_SluiceGate
display_name: Taking the Water Away From the Brine Maw
setup: The basin is brim-full because the Harbor Board pumps were switched off three days ago, deliberately, to flood the Annex's lower doors. The Brine Maw owns that water and takes no damage at all in it. The sluice capstan on the west wall has had its wheel cut off the chain and carried to the bell tower, so the player arrives with KEY_C2_SluiceWheel already in hand and the gate is a plan rather than a mid-boss scavenger hunt.
solution: Ship the wheel on the capstan, then land three full turns, one per pass of the Maw, taking cover behind the capstan housing between passes. The basin drops a third per turn to mud. Beached, the Maw cannot turn and the glowing sac behind its jaw hinge stays exposed on its left flank: two flare rounds into the sac kill it.
failure: Shooting it in deep water deals zero damage. Standing on the low dock for more than one pass is an instant grab kill; the stone quay is safe. Being hit while cranking loses the current turn's progress and about a third of health but not the turn count. If the player has no flares the pistol can finish it slowly, but after 45 s beached it works back into the channel, re-floods the basin to a third, and one turn must be re-cranked. Death respawns at the vestry safe room with the turn count preserved.
hint_1: Shooting it in deep water is just noise. The basin is the only thing on your side down there, so change it.
hint_2: The capstan is on the west wall with the notice bolted to it. Ship the wheel from the bell tower and it's three full turns against the stop.
hint_3: One turn per pass, that's all you get. When it beaches, the sac behind the jaw comes open. Put a flare in it.
hint_trigger: Hint 1 after 20 s of no-damage shooting in deep water. Hint 2 after 45 s in the encounter or one death. Hint 3 after two turns done plus 30 s without progress, or two deaths.

Name: PZL_C3_KeycardB2
setup: Owen's Level B2 keycard swipes and the panel only flashes orange. The reader has lost its conduit plug in the grey wall box left of the bulkhead frame; seat the plug, then swipe, then survive a ten-second reset beep that draws two Husks down the corridor.
solution: Open the grey wall box and push the loose conduit plug home (two interacts, a click each), then swipe KEY_C3_KeycardB2 at the reader and hold the corridor for the 10 s reset. The bulkhead cycles open.
failure: No hard fail. Swiping with the plug loose only chirps the panel and makes a small noise ping. Being grabbed during the reset cancels it and it must be redone; running during the reset leaves two roused Husks loose in the lab corridor.
hint_1: The card's good, I watched it light the panel orange. So it isn't the card.
hint_2: There's a snag list back in the labs that moans about this exact reader. Grey wall box, left of the frame.
hint_3: Open the box, push the loose plug in until it clicks twice, then swipe. And watch the corridor, the reset beeps for ages.
hint_trigger: hint_1 at 60 s idle or 1 failed swipe; hint_2 at 120 s or 3 failed swipes; hint_3 at 200 s or 4 failed swipes

Name: PZL_C3_WhiteboardCode
setup: The B2 security office is a special room behind a four-digit keypad. The security chief, tired of being asked, wrote his hint on a sticky note stuck to the lab whiteboard frame, because the board is where staff stood around.
solution: The whiteboard header reads TRIAL 07 / RUN 03. The sticky note says trial number then run number, two digits each. Enter 0703 on the keypad to open the security office, which holds KEY_C3_MasterKey and the shipment clearance countersigned by W. Hale.
failure: Three wrong codes trip a tamper buzzer: a 15 s red-screen lockout and a loud noise event that pulls the security wing's patrolling Brute to the door. The code never changes and attempts are never capped.
hint_1: Four digits and a note from a man who thought he was being funny. It's on the board.
hint_2: Read the top line of the whiteboard, not the table. Trial number, then run number.
hint_3: Trial seven, run three. Two digits each. Zero seven, zero three.
hint_trigger: hint_1 at 45 s at the keypad or 1 wrong entry; hint_2 at 120 s or 2 wrong entries; hint_3 at 240 s or 4 wrong entries

Name: PZL_C3_CoolantValves
setup: The cold vault is behind an interlock that only releases once the neighbouring cooling chamber has been taken through a complete V-7 cold-shock ladder. Three hand valves on the gallery: 1 BRINE INTAKE (floods to +4 C), 2 CRYO (takes a flooded chamber to -12 C, dead on a dry chamber), 3 PURGE (dumps the chamber and ends the run). A gauge shows chamber temperature with a green HOLD lamp that lights at the stage temperature and goes dark when the hold is served. Two Drowned lie in the chamber sump and are killed by the cryo stage.
solution: Run the four-stage cold-shock ladder in order, serving every hold: stage 1 Valve 1 INTAKE to +4 C, hold 90 s; stage 2 Valve 2 CRYO to -12 C, hold 30 s; stage 3 close CRYO and reopen Valve 1 INTAKE back to +4 C, hold 60 s; stage 4 Valve 3 PURGE. In-game hold times play at quarter speed (about 22 s / 8 s / 15 s). The interlock releases the cold vault. The identical ladder (4 C, -12 C, 4 C, purge) is what the Chapter 5 synthesis machine demands, gated on FLG_C3_ColdShockKnown.
failure: Purging before stage 4, opening CRYO on a dry chamber, or turning any valve before the HOLD lamp goes dark trips the relief vent: 4 s of live steam across the gallery (Caution-level contact damage and a screen whiteout), the gauge drops to ambient and the run resets to stage 1. Unlimited retries; each failed run spawns one extra Drowned up the gallery stair.
hint_1: The vault's holding its own door shut. It wants the chamber run properly first.
hint_2: That log you copied down. Four stages, plus four, minus twelve, plus four, purge. The gauge is the board, the valves are the pen.
hint_3: Intake until the lamp dies, cryo until it dies, shut cryo and intake again until it dies, then purge. Purge last or the vent blows.
hint_trigger: hint_1 on entering the gallery or 60 s idle; hint_2 on the first relief vent trip or 150 s; hint_3 on the second trip or 300 s

Name: PZL_C3_WardenArena
display_name: The Warden: Gas, Doors and a Fuel Line
setup: The coolant plant floor is four hazard-striped bays with three yellow gas valves and four droppable blast doors. The Warden's plate shrugs off pistol and rifle fire from the front; a weeping fuel line under his back plate is the only soft thing on him, and only a gas flash in a sealed bay can strip that plate.
solution: Open a bay's gas valve (6 s to fill), draw the Warden into that bay with noise or with yourself, then pull the bay lever so the blast door traps the gas with him. Fuel off his own pack ignites it on the hot pipe run, buckling his back plate and exposing the fuel line for 4 s. Shoot the line. Three exposures kill him; after the second he blocks one valve, so each cycle must use a different bay.
failure: Standing in a bay when it flashes is heavy damage and a knockdown, lethal from Danger health. Sealing an empty bay wastes its gas and costs 20 s of recharge. All three bays spent at once forces a dodging phase until a valve recharges. Death reloads at the arena entry with doors open and gas reset.
hint_1: Pistol's doing nothing to that plate. Use the room.
hint_2: Yellow gas valves on the bay walls. Open one, get him standing in it, then drop the blast door on the bay.
hint_3: The blast strips his back plate. There's a fuel line under it. Shoot the line while it's bare, you've got about four seconds.
hint_trigger: hint_1 after 25 s of front-plate fire with no weak-point hit; hint_2 at 60 s or after the first wasted bay; hint_3 at 100 s or the first missed 4 s window

Name: PZL_C3_UndertowRaft
setup: A spline set-piece through a field of rock pillars to the cave mouth. Mara rows and steers, Leon kneels at the bow with rifle and flare gun. The player's two verbs are calling the turn (left or right, which is the steering input routed through Mara's rowing stroke) and shooting the eye when the hooded ridge opens.
solution: Phase 1: call left or right to clear alternating pillar pairs and shoot the eye in the 3 s it surfaces before each tentacle swing, which cancels the swing. Phase 2: it grips the gunwale and the eye closes; put five rifle rounds or one flare into the coiled arm to break the grip while Mara bails. Phase 3: it rises across the cave mouth with the eye wide; sustained fire into the open eye over a 12 s window, a flare counting for four rifle rounds, and it sinks under the raft as the current carries them out.
failure: A missed pillar call costs a third of the hull; hull at zero in phase 1 or 2, or too little damage in phase 3, capsizes the raft, with a short drowning cut and a reload to the phase start. Checkpoints at each phase start, and ammunition is topped up at each checkpoint so the player is never dry in a fight they cannot leave.
hint_1: I can't steer and watch. Call it or we're on the rocks.
hint_2: It opens that eye before it swings. That's your window, not after.
hint_3: If it's got hold of the raft, shoot the arm, not the eye. Free us first.
hint_trigger: hint_1 after 2 missed pillar calls; hint_2 after 3 eye surfacings with no hit; hint_3 at 8 s into phase 2 with the arm untouched

Name: PZL_C4_EvidenceKey
setup: The evidence room key is missing from the duty board. The archive holds a personal records cabinet of forty unlocked drawers with brass letter plates, one per serving officer by surname, in a room with two Husks and one twitching corpse that can rise as a Reborn.
solution: The duty log shows Officer Ruiz signed the evidence room key out at 01:12 and never returned it, and body camera clip B shows her dropping it into her own drawer. Drawers are filed by surname letter, so open drawer R.
failure: No hard failure. Every wrong drawer makes noise: two wrong pulls raise the Husks' hearing check, the third brings them to the cabinet, the fourth rises the Reborn. The key never moves.
hint_1: Nobody hid that key, Leon. Somebody filed it. Think like the woman who filed it.
hint_2: The duty log has her name on the evidence key at one twelve, and the cabinet card says one drawer per officer, by surname.
hint_3: Ruiz. R. Pull the R drawer and stop being thorough about it.
hint_trigger: Hint 1 at 60 s in the archive with no drawer opened; hint 2 at 2 wrong drawers or 2 min; hint 3 at 4 wrong drawers or 3 min 30 s.

Name: PZL_C4_PrintMatch
setup: Locker 17 in the evidence room is under a court seal whose electronic bolt releases only from the PrintLock pad on Det. Sgt. Ferris's desk in CID. The player carries one sleeve of three booking print cards and must choose which to lay on the glass.
solution: The pad's standby screen registers right index, WHORL, ridge count 14, accepted 14 Sep. Only card 2, FERRIS M., is a whorl with ridge count 14, and Ferris was booked on 14 Sep on a complaint withdrawn the same day. Lay Ferris's card on the glass and the bolt on locker 17 drops; open the locker by hand downstairs.
failure: A wrong card is rejected. Three wrong reads lock the pad for 90 s and sound the desk alarm, spawning two Husks into the CID corridor. The lockout expires on its own, so the puzzle cannot dead-end.
hint_1: A sealed locker that only opens from a desk upstairs. Somebody wanted exactly one person able to open it.
hint_2: The pad is telling you what it will accept. Right index, whorl, fourteen ridges. You're carrying three cards, read the tops of them.
hint_3: The detective's own card. Ferris. Hale had him printed to scare him and left the one print that opens his own locker sitting in evidence.
hint_trigger: Hint 1 at 45 s at the pad; hint 2 at 1 wrong read or 1 min 30 s; hint 3 at 2 wrong reads or 3 min.

Name: PZL_C4_SafeCode
setup: A four-digit dial safe behind an oak panel in the chief's office holds the revolver and the brass interceptor key, which is the only route out of the station. The code is written nowhere; it is a reading rule applied to the payments ledger the player is carrying.
solution: Hale's diary gives the rule: the money that stayed, the lead figure off each, oldest first, four digits. The ledger's CLEARED rows in date order are 02 Apr 7,500, 19 May 2,000, 23 Aug 4,000 and 14 Sep 1,500, so the code is 7241. The two RETURNED rows, 8,000 and 9,250, are decoys that would give six digits and will not fit the dial.
failure: No lockout and no damage; a wrong code clicks and resets the dial. The ledger is re-readable from the pause menu, so the puzzle can be stalled but never failed. Opening the safe always fires Hale's confession, so the story cannot be skipped past.
hint_1: He wrote a whole page about not writing it down. That page is the instructions.
hint_2: Not the dates, not the reference numbers. The money that stayed. Four of the six cleared, and he wants the first figure off each, oldest first.
hint_3: Seven thousand five, two thousand, four thousand, one thousand five. Seven, two, four, one. Try it.
hint_trigger: Hint 1 at 60 s at the dial or 2 wrong entries; hint 2 at 2 min or 4 wrong entries; hint 3 at 4 min or 7 wrong entries.

Name: PZL_C4_BasementPower
setup: The flooded long store has a leaking floor conduit cast into the slab. Breaker panels A and B sit on the dry walkway with a red interlock lamp between them. Energising the ring electrifies the water, which is the only reliable way to open Chief Hale's guarded chest cavity.
solution: Throw panel A then panel B within 4 seconds, with Hale standing in the water and Leon on the walkway or the stair. The ring fires for 3 s, his limbs lock back in an arch and the chest cavity stays open about 5 s. Three cycles of cavity fire kill him.
failure: More than 4 s between panels trips the interlock: both levers spring up and need 12 s to reset. Standing in the water when the ring fires does heavy damage to Leon and stuns him. Firing the ring while Hale is on the far concrete plinth wastes the cycle.
hint_1: Leon, those panels on the walkway. Read the fault card again.
hint_2: Both of them, together, or the interlock throws it back. And not while you're in the water.
hint_3: Get him out into the middle, get yourself on the walkway, then A and B straight after each other. His chest opens when the limbs pull in.
hint_trigger: Hint 1 at 45 s of the fight with no panel thrown; hint 2 at 90 s or one tripped interlock; hint 3 at 3 min or two tripped interlocks.

Name: PZL_C5_LiftOverride
setup: The tower is in level 3 containment: passenger lifts dead, stairwells shuttered. The freight lift wants a four-digit duty engineering override on a keypad inside the car.
solution: Enter 3042, the lift car's inspection number from the foil sticker inside the car. Not 1987, the year on the lobby plaque.
failure: A wrong code is announced over the lobby PA, which brings the two security Husks back through the shutters, and the keypad locks out for 10 seconds per wrong entry. Entering 1987 gets its own drier refusal line.
hint_1: Four digits on a keypad, and a building full of people who write things down. Somebody told somebody that code.
hint_2: Read the facilities email on the reception terminal again. She says she moved it to the lift car's inspection number.
hint_3: It's the sticker inside the car, at your shoulder. Three zero four two. Not the year on the plaque.
hint_trigger: Hint 1 after 60 s at the keypad or 1 wrong entry; hint 2 after 2 min or 2 wrong entries; hint 3 after 3 min 30 s or 4 wrong entries.

Name: PZL_C5_Sequencer
setup: Antidote component B sits in a cold drawer inside the Genetics vault, a special room on floor 31. The vault door has three thumbwheels, each cycling the bases A, C, G, T, read left to right.
solution: Set the three dials to G, T, C, left to right: the V-7 marker printed on every vial label in the building, loaded in the order Calder's requisition specifies.
failure: A wrong triplet throws the vault's cold alarm: strobe, cold vent, a 25-second window in which two Husks arrive from the open-plan benches, and a 15-second dead bolt on the door. Spawns come from a capped pool.
hint_1: Three dials, three letters. That's a code they used every day, so it'll be printed on something they handled every day.
hint_2: The tech's last page said it's on the labels. Pick a vial off the bench rack and read the marker line.
hint_3: G, T, C. Left to right, the way Calder's requisition says to load the drawer.
hint_trigger: Hint 1 after 90 s or 1 wrong triplet; hint 2 after 3 min or 2 wrong triplets; hint 3 after 4 min 30 s or 4 wrong triplets.

Name: PZL_C5_CryoRack
setup: Antidote component C is clamped in a cryo rack on floor 33. The interlock reads bays 31, 32 and 33 as one set and lifts only when all three agree. Leon finds them at minus 80, minus 20 and OFF, with bay 33's compressor tripped.
solution: Hit the reset button on bay 33's flank, then set all three bay dials to minus 80. The rack lifts.
failure: Any bay left at minus 196 cracks the frost line: a loud alarm at the loading bay that calls the two Brutes in early, and the rack stays shut. Bays left at OFF or minus 20 just hold the interlock lamp amber, so the player is slowed, never hard-blocked.
hint_1: Three bays, three different temperatures, and a rack that won't open. It's not asking you to be clever, it's asking you to be tidy.
hint_2: The cryo log says the interlock reads all three bays as one set. Somebody left one thawing and another one tripped out.
hint_3: Reset bay 33's compressor, then put all three to minus eighty. Not lower. Minus one ninety-six cracks the line and screams.
hint_trigger: Hint 1 after 90 s in the bay room; hint 2 after 3 min or 1 wrong set; hint 3 after 4 min, 2 wrong sets, or immediately after the minus 196 alarm.

Name: PZL_C5_Synthesis
setup: Voss's rig in the Crown Lab: three carrier ports and a keypad. It will not arm with an empty port and rejects any inactivation sequence it does not recognise. The cycle runs 90 seconds with the hood down and cannot be interrupted.
solution: Load component A from the Annex (KEY_C3_AntidoteA), B and C into their ports, then key in the cold-shock sequence found in the Annex trial log (see Chapter 3), gated on FLG_C3_ColdShockKnown. Press RUN and hold the lab for 90 seconds against three Husk waves, then draw the dose.
failure: A missing component: the rig refuses to arm and names the empty port. A wrong sequence: rejected, vents, 20-second lockout. Leon dying during the cycle: checkpoint restores to the moment RUN was pressed with ports loaded and sequence accepted, so the retry is of the fight, not the puzzle.
hint_1: Three ports, three carriers. It won't even arm until all three are in.
hint_2: Then it wants the inactivation sequence. His own sheet says it only ever existed in one place, and you've already been there.
hint_3: The cold-shock sequence from the Annex trial log, Leon. Owen's floor. Key it in exactly as it was written and hit RUN.
hint_trigger: Hint 1 after 45 s at the rig with any port empty; hint 2 after 60 s at the keypad with all ports loaded; hint 3 after 2 min or 2 rejected sequences.

Name: PZL_C5_WaterMain
setup: The roof plant room after the boss. Three brass handles, PURGE, RESERVOIR BYPASS and CITY MAIN, plus a pump switch. The loop still holds about 400 litres of Voss's concentrate, and his timer is counting to 06:12.
solution: Open PURGE and hold it until the sump gauge clears, shut RESERVOIR BYPASS, open CITY MAIN, then start the pump. In that order.
failure: Not a game over. Opening CITY MAIN early starts the concentrate moving; Mara catches it on the north readout within four seconds and shouts. Shutting it inside that window costs nothing. Riding it out forces a checkpoint reload at the plant room door with hint 3 already playing. Skipping the purge flushes the concentrate to the reservoir branch and the pump refuses to run until the loop is clear.
hint_1: Three handles and a pump switch. Get the order wrong and you send his batch instead of yours.
hint_2: The mechanic wrote the order on his work order downstairs, and Voss copied it onto the clipboard right there. Clear the loop first.
hint_3: Purge. Then shut the reservoir bypass. Then open the city main, then the pump. In that order, Leon.
hint_trigger: Hint 1 after 30 s in the plant room; hint 2 after 70 s or 1 wrong handle; hint 3 after 2 min, 2 wrong handles, or any concentrate movement.
